newsitem.title: UK: IBCA rates Investicni a Postovni Banka.
newsitem.headline: IBCA rates Investicni a Postovni Banka.

text.p: IBCA, the European rating agency, said on Wednesday it had assigned Investicni a Postovni Banka (IPB), a long-term rating of BBB and a short-term rating of A2.
At the same time, IBCA said it assigned the bank an individual rating of D and a legal rating of 2.

"IPB is the Czech Republic's third largest bank in terms of total assets and was created out of the merger between Investicni Banka and the Post Office Savings Bank at the start of 1994," IBCA said in a statement.
Investicni Banka itself was established in 1990, primarily to take over the long-term loans to "non-commercial organisations" of the former Czechoslovak State Bank.
"IPB is developing into a universal bank and it has the most extensive branch network of any bank in the Czech Republic thanks to its approximately 3,500 outlets at post offices," IBCA said.
It said the bank had 11 percent and 13 percent shares of Czech deposits and lending at end-1995.

"The government has recently announced its intention to sell its remaining 31.5 percent stake in IPB to a foreign financial institution; a significant proportion of the other shares are controlled by the bank's management and related parties."

The rating agency said the legal and securities ratings primarily reflected IBCA's opinion that, given the bank's importance to the Czech economy, and the recent decision of the Czech National Bank to support the fifth largest bank in the country, IPB would receive support from the state.

"However, the individual and securities ratings are also affected by concerns about IPB's rapid balance sheet growth in recent years, its weak asset quality, its large portfolio of investments in Czech companies and lack of transparency in its corporate governance," IBCA said. "Although the bank had an unconsolidated capital ratio of 10.81 percent at end-June 1996, this is likely to need strengthening given its current risk profile and rapid expansion."
